classification.difficultyReason: Translate square-root variation into an equation, determine the constant from measured values, and substitute a new length while retaining precision.

content.prompt: In a special type of pendulum, called a conical pendulum, the time taken to complete one oscillation, which is called the period $P$, varies directly with the square-root of the length $L$ of the pendulum.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write this algebraically using $k$ as the constant of proportionality.

answer.worked: Direct variation with $\sqrt{L}$ gives $P=k\sqrt{L}$, where $k$ is the constant of proportionality.

children.label: b
children.prompt: When the length of the pendulum is $L=0.29\text{ m}$ the period is $P=1.005\text{ s}$. What will be the period of a conical pendulum with length $L=2\text{ m}$? Give your answer in seconds rounded to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}1.005&=k\sqrt{0.29}\\k&=\frac{1.005}{\sqrt{0.29}}\end{align*}$$
For $L=2\text{ m}$, retaining the unrounded value of $k$:
$$\begin{align*}P&=\frac{1.005}{\sqrt{0.29}}\sqrt{2}\\P&=2.639259\ldots\text{ s}\\P&\approx2.64\text{ s}\quad\text{(2 decimal places)}\end{align*}$$
